findings: Three Intel 6975P-C hosts reproduce the iterator-only and full-candidate AArch64 raw cycle increase with unchanged retired instruction counts.
DSB-to-MITE penalty-cycle ratios increase to 2.57-2.62 for iterator-only and 2.57-2.61 for full candidate. A/A and added-leaf-only controls do not show that increase.
Both DSB and MITE delivered-uop counts rise despite unchanged retired instruction counts. This motivates retired-fusion and issued-versus-retired measurements.
Critical DSB-miss PEBS event is unsupported on all capable hosts; no inference is made from that missing event.
limits: Speculative events and cycles overlap. The approximately 8 million additional switch penalty cycles cannot be added to or equated with the approximately 3.4 million net cycle increase. This evidence supports a frontend layout effect, not a complete microarchitectural attribution or an alignment fix.
followup: R1477 preserves the same frozen binaries and measures retired fusion/slots, issued uops, and cycle hotspots while resolving each report against its matching executable.
